body:
marek: quick heads-up — we need to finalise the geo-probe heuristics before next week's rollout. current probe bursts are spiking cost on low-tier tenants.

julia: saw that on staging this morning. telemetry shows concentrated probes right after a cold-start. looks like zero splay on tenant-level probes. :grimacing:

samir: is this the per-region reachability probe or the route-compat check?

marek: both. we run short liveness probes + full compatibility probes when a route changes. compatibility probes are heavier and we currently schedule them synchronously across all regions for a tenant.

anya: that sync pattern is the root cause. when we flip a rollout flag, all regions try to validate and rewarm caches at once => probe storm + cost amplification.

marek: proposal: introduce a degradation-splay window and per-tenant probe budget. splay should be proportional to num_regions^0.8 and budget should be a token bucket.

julia: +1. also we should prefer incremental checks: small binary compatibility pings first, only escalate to full model probe if binary passes.

samir: rough config idea:```yaml
probe:
  compatibility:
    base_interval: 60s
    splay: 180s  # max jitter applied across regions
    escalation_threshold: 3  # small passes before heavy probe
  tenant_budget:
    tokens_per_hour: 120
    refill_rate: 2rpm
```

anya: looks good. edge case: what if telemetry is stale and we think a region is healthy but it isn't? we might delay a needed probe. need a freshness TTL and forced probe if last good >= TTL.

marek: agree. TTL should be conservative for hosted high-tier tenants (short TTL) and more lenient for free/low-tier. suggestion: tier->ttl mapping.

julia: we also need a canary path: when rollout touches a new model, pick a single warm region to run the heavy compatibility probe first, then spread if it succeeds. avoids repeated rollbacks.

samir: adding probabilistic backoff for retries helps too: if a probe fails, exponentially backoff with jitter and decrement tenant budget less for retries to avoid double-penalty.

infra-bot: deploy-check results: probe-heuristics-v2 tests passing (5/5), cost-sanity failing on synthetic-large-tenants. See <https://ci.redwood.example/runs/7821>

anya: CI fail expected until we add splay + tenant budget. CI uses synthetic tenant with 50 regions — we should cap test tenants or simulate splay in tests.

marek: one more thought — telemetry lag can mask distributed failures. add line in Console that surfaces 'probe debt' per tenant (queued probes vs allowed budget). ops can preemptively throttle rollouts.

julia: UI surface is important. if an enterprise customer sees cost spikes we want fast rollback + visibility. add a feature-flag to opt-out of full compatibility probes during rollout.

samir: action items: 1) implement splay + tenant token bucket 2) escalate-first-light-probe then heavy 3) add TTL per-tier 4) CI test update to model splay 5) console probe-debt dashboard.

marek: i'll write a short RFC with config defaults and a sample rollout plan. will include the YAML snippet and math for splay sizing (regions^0.8). aim to merge before next Tuesday's deploy.

anya: ping me on the RFC — I'll draft the console mockups.

julia: i'll update the integration tests to simulate splay.

marek: thanks — tl;dr: avoid synchronized heavy probes, add splay + budgets + TTLs + canary-first. :thumbsup:
